The moderator plays an important role of injecting new directions into the discourse. To generate the moderator’s utterance, Co-STORM instructs the LM to generate informed questions based on the uncited sources retrieved since the last moderator turn. To choose among the many uncited sources, the moderator reranks each piece of information i based on the similarity to the topic t and the dissimilarity to its associated question q. Formally, the reranking score is     cos(i, t)α(1− cos(i,q))1−α,     where i, t,q are corresponding text embeddings and α is a hyperparameter. This reranking func- tion prioritizes information that does not directly answer the original question but is relevant to the topic t. Co-STORM concatenates these reranked sources along with concept names in C to avoid repetitive concepts. This combined context is used to prompt the LM to generate the question for the moderator turn and an updated list of experts, P ′.     4 Co-STORM Implementation     The LM component of Co-STORM is implemented using zero-shot prompting via the DSPy framework (Khattab et al., 2023) and gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (see full prompts in Appendix D). In the previous AI Regulation of 2020, in addition to risk assessment, there was still the topic of "ecosystem of excellence", which dealt with the research and development potential of AI. In the present regulation 2023, this theme is now non-binding and hardly implemented by member states. It is impossible to see how the EU intends to catch up with the world leaders in AI innovation (e.g. USA, Switzerland, South Korea, China). The lack of coordination between industry and university research, but also the European fragmentation of education systems, add to this. Together with restrictive data protection, the EU could thus increasingly fall further behind. In addition, experience has shown that different interpretations in the EU countries could increase legal uncertainty. There is already the slogan abroad concerning AI: Other countries invests to become attractive, the EU regulates.
